subject: geography
title: Ecosystems Adventure: Global Biomes
welcome_lead: From scorching deserts to icy tundra — climate controls where the great biomes live.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography Global biomes — rainforest, desert, tundra, savanna, deciduous forest.
final_note: You can now locate the major world biomes and explain why they're where they are.

concepts.def: Large region with similar climate, plants and animals
Hot wet biome near the equator — huge biodiversity
Dry biome ~30°N/S — under high pressure belts
Tropical grassland with wet and dry seasons
Temperate biome — trees drop leaves in winter

walkthroughs.body_html:
The sun's energy hits the equator most directly — hot and wet here.

At ~30°N and 30°S, sinking dry air creates the world's great deserts (Sahara, Atacama, Australian outback).

Towards the poles, biomes get colder: deciduous forest → coniferous (taiga) → tundra → ice.

Near the equator (Amazon, Congo, SE Asia).

Hot (25-30°C year-round) and wet (>2000mm rain). Layered structure: emergents, canopy, under-canopy, forest floor.

Contains over 50% of the world's terrestrial species despite covering only ~6% of land.

Found ~30° latitude (Sahara, Arabia, Mojave) under permanent high pressure.

Less than 250mm rainfall per year. Huge temperature range — scorching day, freezing night.

Plants (cacti) have waxy skin and deep roots. Animals are often nocturnal.

mcqs.q: Why are the world's great hot deserts found around 30°N and 30°S?
options: Sinking dry air from high pressure belts

mcqs.q: Which biome is characterised by PERMAFROST?

numericals.q: Approximately what maximum annual rainfall (mm) defines a hot desert?
numericals.hint: Less than a quarter of a metre per year.

free_texts.q: Which tropical biome with wet and dry seasons covers much of central Africa and is famous for lions and acacia trees? One word.
